Rashi on Niddah 59a:12:1.hebrew: לא להקל על דברי תורה - האי דגזור רבנן בכתמים להחמיר על ד"ת, שלא להקל בנדה גמורה. ומיהו כתמים עצמן דרבנן, ואזלינן בהן לקולא ותלינן בכל מידי:
Rashi on Niddah 59a:12:1.english: Not to be lenient regarding Torah law - That which the Rabbis decreed regarding stains was to be stringent beyond Torah law, so as not to be lenient regarding a full niddah. However, stains themselves are rabbinic, and [therefore] we rule leniently regarding them and attribute [them] to anything [possible].

Rashi on Niddah 59a:14:1.english: An elongated stain combines - To [the size of] a split bean and more.

Rashi on Niddah 59a:14:2.hebrew: משוך כל דהו טמא - דכיון דאמר משוך מגופה אתי, ובמשיכה תליא טעמא, אפילו בכחרדל טמא:
Rashi on Niddah 59a:14:2.english: An elongated [stain of] whatever size is impure - For since he said that an elongated [stain] comes from her body, and the reason depends on [its] elongation, even [if it is as small as] a mustard seed, it is impure.

Rashi on Niddah 59a:15:1.english: Actually - Even according to Rabbi Eliezer, it requires combination.

Rashi on Niddah 59a:15:2.english: And when Rabbi Eliezer said - An elongated [stain] certainly flowed down from her body.

Rashi on Niddah 59a:15:3.english: On an examination cloth - With which she examines herself.

Rashi on Niddah 59a:15:4.hebrew: אבל בכתם - שעל חלוקה, כגריס ועוד בעינן:
Rashi on Niddah 59a:15:4.english: But with regard to a stain - Which is on her tunic, we require [the size of] a split bean and more.

Rashi on Niddah 59a:1:1.english: Drops of blood below - That is to say, small [drops].

Rashi on Niddah 59a:1:3.english: [The size of] a split bean and below - [That is,] as less than [the size of] a split bean, and we attribute [it].

Rashi on Niddah 59a:2:1.english: [If] there was found on her the size of a split bean and more - For the halakha is in accordance with Rav Ḥisda, who is lenient [that she may attribute a stain the size of a split bean to a louse].

Rashi on Niddah 59a:3:1.hebrew: כיון דבעלמא - היכא דליכא ועוד, תליא כגריס במאכולת, השתא נמי תליא האי גריס במאכולת אחרינא:
Rashi on Niddah 59a:3:1.english: Since in general - Where there is no "and more" [excess], she attributes [a stain the size of] a split bean to a louse; now too, she attributes this [remaining] split bean to another louse.

Rashi on Niddah 59a:4:1.english: She was occupied with [an amount] the size of a split bean - [Such as] the blood of a bird or eye salve.

Rashi on Niddah 59a:5:1.hebrew: אבל הכא דנתעסקה תליא - כגריס בדם צפור, ועוד דם מאכולת הוה:
Rashi on Niddah 59a:5:1.english: But here, where she was occupied, she attributes [it] - [She attributes] the [size of a] split bean to the blood of a bird, and the excess was the blood of a louse.

Rashi on Niddah 59a:7:1.hebrew: מאי למימרא - הא אפילו תליא כגריס בצפור, אכתי פש ליה גריס ועוד:
Rashi on Niddah 59a:7:1.english: What is [the purpose of] stating [this] - For even if she attributes [the size of] a split bean to the bird, there still remains [the size of] a split bean and more.

Rashi on Niddah 59a:8:1.hebrew: מהו דתימא - שקול כגריס דם צפור, ושדי בי מצעי:
Rashi on Niddah 59a:8:1.english: Lest you say - Take [the size of] a split bean of bird's blood and cast [it] into the middle.

Rashi on Niddah 59a:9:1.hebrew: נמצא עליה מין אחד - מדבר הדומה לכתם, כגון קילור או שרף, ואחר כך מצאה על חלוקה כתם — אפי' אין מראיתו דומה לאותו המין, תולה בו:
Rashi on Niddah 59a:9:1.english: One type was found on her - Of a substance resembling a stain, such as eye salve or sap, and afterward she found a stain on her tunic — even if its appearance does not resemble that type, she attributes [it] to it.

Rashi on Niddah 59a:9:2.hebrew: נתעסקה שאני - דכיון דנתעסקה במין אדום, היכי תלינן ביה כתם שחור? אבל נמצא עליה מין אדום, תולה בה כתם שחור, דאמרינן: כי היכי דניתן עליה האי מין בדלא ידעה, הכי נמי הוה עלה מינא אחרינא ולא ידעה:
Rashi on Niddah 59a:9:2.english: [Where] she was occupied is different - For since she was occupied with a red substance, how could we attribute a black stain to it? But [if] a red substance was found on her, she may attribute a black stain to it, for we say: Just as this substance got onto her without her knowledge, so too another substance was on her without her knowledge.

Tosafot on Niddah 59a:1:1.hebrew: היו בה טיפי דמים למטה וטיפי דמים למעלה תלינן בעליון עד כגריס - פ"ה: למטה — קטנים, למעלה — גדולים, תלינן בעליון הגדול בדם מאכולת עד כגריס. מאי לאו עד כגריס כלמטה, בפחות מכגריס? לא, כלמעלה, ביותר מכגריס. וזהו תימה: אמאי נקט למעלה ולמטה? הוה ליה למנקט גדולים וקטנים! ועוד, היכי משמע ליה כלמטה, מאי אולמיה ממתניתין? ועוד, דלא הוה ליה למנקט כלמעלה וכלמטה, דהוה ליה למימר כפחות מכגריס ויותר מכגריס, לישנא דנקט עד הכא! ונראה לי דה"פ: למטה — למטה מן החגור, למעלה — למעלה מן החגור. תולה בעליון — אותו שלמטה נתלה בעליון, דשמא כמו שעליון מעלמא אתי, תחתון נמי מעלמא אתי, ועוד כגריס נתלה בו. וקאמר: מאי לאו כגריס למטה — דעד כגריס דקתני מיירי שהתחתון עד כגריס תולה בעליון, שממקום שבא העליון בא התחתון; מכלל דאי לאו עליון, מטמינן ליה ולא תלינן בדם מאכולת, אלמא כגריס כיותר מכגריס! ומשני: לא, כגריס ולמעלה. כלומר, תולה תחתון בעליון כשהעליון עד כגריס, ומלמעלה למטה קחשיב, כשהעליון ג' גריסין או שני גריסין עד כגריס — שאז אין אנו תולין עליון בדם מאכולת אלא מעלמא אתי — אז נתלה בו התחתון, ומיירי כשתחתון יותר מכגריס. אבל אם היה העליון כגריס, אז לא יהיה התחתון טהור, שאין רגלים לדבר דאתא דם בה מעלמא, שהרי העליון יש לתלותו בדם מאכולת:
Tosafot on Niddah 59a:1:1.english: If there were drops of blood on her below and drops of blood above, we attribute [it] to the upper one up to the size of a split bean - Rashi explained: "Below" [means] small [drops], [and] "above" [means] large [drops]; we attribute [the stain] to the upper, large [drop as being] the blood of a louse, up to [the size of] a split bean (kigris). Does it not mean [that a drop] up to a kigris is like the "lower" [category], [meaning] like less than a kigris? No, [it is] like the "upper" [category], [meaning] like more than a kigris. And this is astonishing: Why did [the baraita] state "above" and "below"? It should have stated "large" and "small"! And furthermore, how did [the Gemara] infer [that it is] like the "lower" [category]? In what way is it stronger than our mishna? And furthermore, [the Gemara] should not have stated "like above" and "like below", for it should have said "like less than a kigris" and "more than a kigris" — the terminology that it used up until now! And it seems to me that this is its explanation: "Below" [means] below the belt; "above" [means] above the belt. "She attributes [it] to the upper one" — the one that is below is attributed to the upper one, for perhaps just as the upper [blood] came from an external source, the lower [blood] also came from an external source; and furthermore, [a drop the size of] a kigris is attributed to it. And [the Gemara] says: Does it not mean that [the drop the size of] a kigris is below? Meaning, that which was taught: "up to a kigris", deals with [a case where] the lower one is up to a kigris, [which] she attributes to the upper one, [reasoning] that from the place that the upper one came, the lower one came; by implication, were it not for the upper one, we would declare her impure and would not attribute [it] to the blood of a louse — thus [proving that] a kigris is like more than a kigris! And [the Gemara] answers: No, [it means] a kigris and above. That is to say, she attributes the lower one to the upper one when the upper one is up to a kigris, and it is reckoning from top to bottom: when the upper one is three grisin or two grisin, down to a kigris — for then we do not attribute the upper one to the blood of a louse, but rather [we say that] it came from an external source — then the lower one is attributed to it; and [the baraita] deals with [a case] where the lower one is more than a kigris. However, if the upper one were [only] a kigris, then the lower one would not be pure, because there is no basis to say that blood came upon her from an external source, as the upper one can be attributed to the blood of a louse.

Tosafot on Niddah 59a:4:1.hebrew: נתעסקה בכגריס ומצאה עליה כגריס ועוד - אור"י: הוא הדין נתעסקה בפחות מכגריס ונמצא עליה כגריס ועוד, דבכלל בעיא זו. דאין לומר דבהא פשיטא ליה דאינה תולה, אפי' לרבי ינאי; דא"כ, כי פשיט לקמן: מאי לאו בכה"ג, לוקמה בשנתעסקה בפחות מכגריס, דפשיטא ליה דאינה תולה. אלא ודאי, בכל ענין בעי:
Tosafot on Niddah 59a:4:1.english: [If] she was occupied with [an item the size of] a split bean and found upon herself [a stain the size of] a split bean and more - Ri says: The same applies [if] she was occupied with less than [the size of] a split bean and there was found upon her [a stain the size of] a split bean and more, that [this case] is included in this dilemma. For one cannot say that in this [case] it was obvious to him that she does not attribute [it], even according to Rabbi Yannai; for if so, when [the Gemara] resolves [the dilemma] below: "Is it not in a case like this?", let it establish [the baraita] as referring to [a case] where she was occupied with less than [the size of] a split bean, where it is obvious to him that she does not attribute [it]! Rather, [Rabbi Yirmeya] certainly raises the dilemma in every case.

Tosafot on Niddah 59a:9:1.hebrew: נמצא עליה מין אחד - פ"ה: מדבר הדומה לכתם, כגון שרף או קילור, דהא ודאי מעלמא אתא — תולה בו כמה מיני כתמים, ואינה מכרת אם דם היא. ור"י מפרש: נמצא — שמצאה מין אחד למעלה מן החגור, תולה בו כמה מינים שלמטה מן החגור; משום שכמו שהעליון ודאי מעלמא אתא, כך נאמר בתחתון דמעלמא אתא:
Tosafot on Niddah 59a:9:1.english: One type was found on her - Rashi explains: [This refers to] a substance resembling a stain, such as sap or eye salve (kilor) — for this certainly came from the outside world — [and] she may attribute several types of stains to it, and she does not recognize whether it is blood. And the Ri explains: "Was found" [means] that she found one type [of stain] above the belt; she may attribute to it several types [found] below the belt, because just as the upper [stain] certainly came from the outside world, so we say regarding the lower [stain] that it came from the outside world.
